enhanced_information: Hyperacute rejection of a transplant is primarily caused by preformed antibodies that lead to immediate recognition of the transplant as foreign, resulting in hyperacute rejection with 95% confidence. CD8 + T lymphocytes can also contribute to hyperacute rejection through direct cytotoxic attack on the transplant with 80% confidence. Circulating immune complexes, despite their potential role in activating the complement cascade, are not the primary cause of hyperacute rejection.
analysis: Hyperacute rejection of a transplant is an immediate and severe form of rejection that occurs within minutes to hours after transplantation. It is primarily caused by preformed antibodies in the recipient's blood that recognize antigens on the transplanted organ.
